language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for

related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.

Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

MINUTES
  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
  NOVEMBER 14, 2022 AT 5:36 PM

Chair Lambillotte requests the commission to end the meeting in memory of Shirak Khojayan. Extends
deepest condolences to Commissioner Khojayan and family.

 1.  ROLL CALL
  PRESENT: Commissioners Broussalian, Khojayan, Lambillotte, and Ex Officio Roth.
  ABSENT: Commissioner Perian, Tatiyants and Ex Officio Gonzalez.

 2.  REGULAR BUSINESS AGENDA
  a. Report of Recorder, re: Posting of Agenda. The Agenda for the November 14, 2022
  Regular Meeting of the Commission on the Status of Women was Posted on
  November 10, 2022, on the Bulletin Board Outside City Hall.

 3.  INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS

  a. YWCA Glendale & Pasadena: Domestic Violence Programs & Services
  Presentation by Elizabeth Sahagun, Director of Domestic Violence Programs and Operations

  Sahagun presented a brief overview of the operations and services provided by the YWCA Shelter
  also known as Sunrise Village Emergency Shelter. Commissioner Khojayan asked how long
  individuals can stay in the shelter and the response was 45 days for people who are actively fleeing
  domestic violence. Commissioner Khojayan asked if individuals receive pantry donations and the
  response was that the hope closet provides clothing, toiletries and food. Commissioner Broussalian
  asked how they address the needs of all the individuals in transitional and permanent housing
  phases and the response was that a housing specialist and housing case manager work with the
  individuals and landlords to help secure housing units. Sahagun stated that 16 total beds are
  available at the shelter for adults and children and that all housing vouchers last a lifetime. She also
  mentioned that some organizations provide clothing drives for the individuals in the shelter and that
  any further donations to the hope closet would be most helpful. Lastly, Sahagun stated that the
  shelter contacts landlords inside and outside the City of Glendale for the securing of available units
  for use by the shelter.
 4.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to items NOT a part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed 5 minutes. The
  Commission may question or respond to the speaker but there will be no debate or discussion.
  Staff may refer the matter to the proper department for investigation and report.

  No comments.

5.  CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the minutes of the regular Commission Meeting held on August 8, 2022

  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Khojayan
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (3-0-0)

6.  ACTION ITEMS
  a. Consideration of Time Change of the Regular Meetings for the Commission on the
  Status of Women
  1. Resolution of the Commission on the Status of Women to Set the Time of Regular
  Meetings

  Motion by Commissioner Khojayan to change the regular meeting time to 4:00pm. Seconded
  by Broussalian
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (3-0-0)

  b. Consideration of Event in Recognition of International Women's Day
  1. Motion to Appoint an Ad Hoc Committee to Plan an Event in March 2023 for International
  Women's Day

  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian to establish the Ad Hoc Committee with Commissioner
  Tatiyants and Ex Officio Roth would serve on to plan an International Women’s Day in
  March 2023 with funding not to exceed $1,000. Seconded by Khojayan.
  Ayes: Commissioner Broussalian, Khojayan, and Chair Lambillottee
  Noes:
  Abstain:
  Motion passes (3-0-0)
 7.  REPORTS-INFORMATION ONLY
  a. Legislative Update: Governor's Action on State Legislation
  Staff member Powers provided an update.
  b. Update on Domestic Violence Awareness Month Activities
  Staff member Powers provided the report.
  c. Update on Sponsorship of Glendale Unified School District Yellow Ribbon Week:
  Hands & Words Are Not For Hurting Project®
  Staff member Powers provided the report.
  d. Update on Strategic Plan
  Staff member Powers provided the report.

8.  COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN/STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Khojayan wishes everyone a Happy Thanksgiving. Chair Lambillottee stated that
  staff member, Powers will be leaving the City of Glendale and presented Powers with a card and
  flowers to thank her for her support of the commission. Staff member Powers stated that
  Commissioner Khojayan is being recognized by the Western Diocese of the Armenian Church on
  November 30th for the continuous dedication, commitment and benevolence to the Armenian
  community.

9.  ADJOURNMENT @ 6:18pm

  Adjournment in memory of Shirak Khojayan.
  Motion by Commissioner Broussalian and seconded by Khojayan.
